hypothesis: V3 Candidate Hypothesis 1: Cross-Instrument Lead-Lag (Relative Strength Rotation)

pre_registered_specification.instruments: EUR_USD (leader, chosen on liquidity grounds before testing), GBP_USD (lagger)
pre_registered_specification.lag: exactly 1 bar (15 minutes) ahead, fixed - not swept
pre_registered_specification.threshold: none - unconditional on magnitude, sign-based decision every bar
pre_registered_specification.no_lookahead: ret_EUR[T] fully known at decision time T (bar T closed); ret_GBP[T+1] strictly in the future at T

sample_size.note: far above the project's 150-trade minimum-sample convention

primary_test_EUR_leads_GBP.interpretation: negative correlation and sub-50% directional accuracy - the OPPOSITE sign from the hypothesis, which predicted GBP catching up in EUR's direction

baseline_A_GBP_own_autocorrelation.description: GBP_USD's own lag-1 return predicting its own next return - the already-rejected single-instrument momentum mechanism

cross_baseline_comparison: Primary test (r=-0.0095), baseline A (r=-0.0300) and baseline B (r=-0.0145) are all negative and similar in magnitude regardless of which instrument 'leads' - consistent with generic microstructure-level negative serial correlation (bid-ask bounce), not a genuine cross-instrument information-flow/catch-up effect specific to EUR->GBP.

stability_by_year.interpretation: sign flips between years (2021 only positive year); no stable, consistently-signed relationship

cost_adjusted_edge.interpretation: raw signal is already slightly negative before any cost; realistic spread cost at 15-minute trade frequency overwhelms any conceivable edge

verdict: REJECTED. Three independent lines of evidence converge: (1) correlation is the wrong sign for the hypothesis and directional accuracy is significantly below 50%, not above it; (2) the effect is statistically indistinguishable in shape/magnitude from generic single-instrument microstructure autocorrelation (both baselines), suggesting no genuine leader-to-lagger information-flow mechanism specific to this pair; (3) even ignoring transaction costs, the raw signal produces slightly negative expected returns, and realistic spread cost makes it decisively negative. This was a single, pre-committed test per the project's no-variant-search discipline - it does not rule out every possible lag/instrument combination, but it failed cleanly rather than ambiguously.
does_not_proceed_to: V3 build - hypothesis rejected at the cheap-falsification stage, before any strategy/entry-exit code was written.
